intro: Today’s AI builds showcase new security agents, voice models, collaborative tools, and visual demos for developers and businesses.

picks.name: Open-Source Cybersecurity Platform
picks.what: An open-source cybersecurity platform that uses AI agents to protect businesses.
picks.why: Shows how AI agents can be applied to security, useful for teams building protective tech.

picks.name: Hurston-1
picks.what: A narrowband TTS model that excels at Southern American and African English accents, released under Apache-2.0.
picks.why: Provides high-quality regional speech synthesis, valuable for developers targeting diverse user voices.

picks.name: Yourcast 2.0
picks.what: AI-generated summaries with tap-to-jump timestamps delivered directly in Telegram.
picks.why: Enables quick content digestion inside a popular messenger, appealing for product teams and creators.

picks.name: AgentGrid.io
picks.what: A shared workspace that lets humans and AI agents collaborate on tasks.
picks.why: Facilitates coordinated human‑agent workflows, interesting for teams building agent‑centric products.

picks.name: Llama Windows
picks.what: Runs a local AI server that integrates with any Windows application.
picks.why: Provides a simple way to add local LLM capabilities to Windows software, useful for developers.

picks.name: whatsmyagentdoing
picks.what: Visual dashboard showing live activity of Claude Code and Codex agents on your machine.
picks.why: Helps developers monitor and debug AI coding assistants, improving productivity.
picks.signal: 226 stars since 23 Oct, written in JavaScript

picks.name: MemT-1.0
picks.what: Repository for MemT-1.0 focusing on long‑context and long‑term memory for LLMs.
picks.why: Offers resources for building memory‑enhanced agents, relevant for researchers and builders.
picks.signal: 398 stars since 19 Oct, written in Python
